To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a 10Gb/s half-rate decision feedback (DFE) equalizer with 2 infinite impulse response (IR) filters and 1 discrete-time tap.
we have designed and fabricated a 10Gb/s DFE with a power consumption of 4.1 mW and a low transmit swing.
we have developed a 4.1 mW 10Gb/s DFE with 24 dB channel equalization in 28nm LP technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a 10Gb/s receiver with low energy per bit and low area.
the development of a low-power and low-complexity DFE for 10Gb/s serial links.
the design and implementation of a half rate DFE in CMOS.

the paper presents a DFE that is able to equalize 24dB of channel loss at the 3dB bandwidth, with 150mV of transmit swing, and consumes 4.1 mW at 10Gb/s.
the DFE is the most efficient equalizer for the high data rate applications, such as 10 GbE, 25 GbE, etc.
the proposed DFE is a low-power, low-voltage, low-complexity solution for high-speed optical communications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 10Gb/s, 4.1 mW DFE is demonstrated in 28nm LP process with 24dB of channel loss at the nyquist frequency.
the 28nm LP process is a viable option for low power high speed serial links.
we have designed a low-power 10 Gb/sec 2-IIR+1-discrete-taps DFE that is suitable to be used in high-end applications such as 10G Ethernet.

it is possible to achieve a high performance, low power DFE with a low transmit signal swing.
a DFE can be implemented using a combination of IIR filters and a single discrete-tap.
